info.title: P2PC API
info.description: The P2PC control plane REST API. Errors are RFC 9457 `application/problem+json` with a stable `code`. Lists use cursor pagination (`limit` ≤ 100, `cursor`).

get.summary: The caller's account's audit events, newest first.

parameters.name: kind
parameters.description: Only events of this kind, for example `key_created`.

403.description: The key lacks the admin scope.

post.summary:
Asks what would happen to a job, without creating it. The body, the header and the validation are those of
`POST /v1/jobs`.
post.description:
`matching_nodes` counts the enrolled nodes that could ever run the job (right pool, labels, a ready sandbox
driver, enough offered capacity and GPUs) and `would_queue` says whether it would wait for room right now (no
matching node is online, connected, not draining and with enough free capacity). With no matching node,
`feasible` is false and `would_queue` true, with a `reason`; a job submitted anyway stays queued, because nothing
expires in v0.1. When the request carries the idempotency key of a job this key already submitted with the same
body, and that job is held in the queue after 10 failed offers (§8 "Offer cap"), `reason` is that job's reason.
`units_per_hour` is the job's cost per hour, in milli-units.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Accepted and validated like in `POST /v1/jobs`; an estimate creates nothing.

403.description: `forbidden`: the key lacks `jobs:read`. `image_not_allowed`: the key may not run the image.

get.summary: Lists the caller's jobs, newest first (`created_at` descending, then `id`), with cursor pagination.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description:
Only jobs in this state: `queued`, `assigned`, `running`, `succeeded`, `failed`, `timed_out`, `cancelled` or
`lost`.

200.description: A page of jobs. `spec.env` values are `<redacted>` and `spec.files` have no content.

403.description: The key lacks `jobs:read`.

post.summary: Submits a job. It is stored `queued` (attempt 1), and the scheduler places it later.
post.description:
- The body is validated with the §7 table; the image is normalized.
- The key's `allowed_images` must cover the normalized image (`403 image_not_allowed`), and its `daily_unit_cap`
  must hold the estimate on top of what the key has reserved today, UTC (`402 cap_exceeded`; exactly at the cap is
  allowed).
- **Idempotency.** The key comes from `idempotency_key` or the `Idempotency-Key` header (if both are given they
  must be equal). The same key with the same request returns the existing job (`200`); with a different request,
  `409 idempotency_conflict`. Two concurrent identical requests create one job. Idempotency keys are scoped to
  the **API key** that submitted the job, and no response ever contains one: another key reusing the same
  idempotency key simply gets its own new job (`201`), so it learns nothing about this one.
- The caller's key is reloaded inside the transaction (§5): a key revoked or expired mid-request gets `401` and
  no job is created.

parameters.name: Idempotency-Key
parameters.description: Makes the submission idempotent; must equal `idempotency_key` if both are given. 1-255 printable ASCII characters.

200.description: This API key already used the idempotency key with the same request: the existing job.

201.description: The job was created and is queued.

401.description: Missing or invalid key, or the key was revoked or expired while the request was in flight.

402.description: `cap_exceeded`: the job's estimate would exceed the key's daily unit cap.

403.description: `forbidden`: the key lacks `jobs:write`. `image_not_allowed`: the key's allowed images do not cover the image.

409.description: `idempotency_conflict`: this API key already used the idempotency key with a different request. (Idempotency keys are scoped to the API key; another key reusing it gets its own job.)

422.description: Invalid job: `errors` lists each field. Codes: `validation_failed`, `unsupported_pool`, `too_large` (the job does not fit its `Lease` frame), `invalid_body`.

get.summary:
One job of the caller, with its `attempts` (§7): `[{attempt, node_id, outcome, reason, started_at, ended_at}]`,
oldest first. `outcome` uses the job-state words (`running` while the attempt is in progress). A job of another
account answers `404`, exactly like one that does not exist (SI-7).

200.description: The job, with its `attempts` (oldest first; refused or unanswered offers are not attempts). `spec.env` values are `<redacted>` and `spec.files` have no content.

403.description: The key lacks `jobs:read`.

404.description: No such job in this account.

post.description:
- `queued`: becomes `cancelled` at once.
- `assigned` or `running`: the status does not change yet. `cancel_requested_at` is set (once), and the scheduler
  delivers the `Cancel` to the node; the job ends `cancelled` when the node reports.
- Already finished: `200` with the job unchanged.

401.description: Missing or invalid key, or the key was revoked or expired while the request was in flight.

403.description: The key lacks `jobs:write`.

404.description: No such job in this account.

get.summary: The NDJSON log of an attempt: `{seq, stream, ts, data}` per line, `data` as UTF-8 with invalid bytes replaced.
get.description:
- **Page** (default): the lines stored now with `seq >= since_seq`. A job with no logs yet gives an empty `200`.
- **Follow** (`follow=true`): the same, then new lines as they are stored; the stream ends once the attempt is
  over and its log is flushed.
- **How the body ends.** A clean end (the HTTP body completes) means the lines asked for are all there: for a follow,
  the attempt is over and its log is flushed. Anything else ends the body with an **error** (the connection is
  cut without the end of the body, so a client sees a broken transfer): after `http.keepalive_idle_ms` (60 s by
  default) with no new line, on a log that cannot be read and on a server error. The client resumes with
  `since_seq = last seq + 1`, losing and repeating nothing.
- At most 64 MiB are stored per attempt; past that, one `stderr` line marks the truncation. That line also has
  the member `truncated: true`, which no job output can produce (readers that do not know it ignore it).

parameters.name: since_seq
parameters.description: The first `seq` to return, inclusive (default 0). Resume with the last `seq` seen plus one.

parameters.name: follow
parameters.description: Keep the stream open and send new lines as they are stored, until the attempt ends (default false).

200.description: NDJSON, one `LogLine` per line, in `seq` order.

403.description: The key lacks `jobs:read`.

404.description: No such job in this account, or no such attempt.

get.summary:
The published output files of an attempt, by path, with their size and sha256. After the retention period the
entries stay, with `expired: true`, and their downloads answer `410`.

403.description: The key lacks `jobs:read`.

404.description: No such job in this account, or no such attempt.

parameters.name: path
parameters.description: The output's path relative to `/outputs`, for example `results/a.csv` (its segments percent-encoded).

X-P2PC-SHA256.description: The file's SHA-256, 64 lowercase hex characters.

403.description: The key lacks `jobs:read`.

404.description: No such job in this account, no such attempt, or no such output.

410.description: `expired`: the output was deleted after the retention period.

get.summary: The caller's account's keys, in creation order, revoked ones included. Never contains a secret.

403.description: The key lacks the admin scope.

post.summary: Creates an API key in the caller's project. The full key is in the response, once.
post.description:
A key can never create a more powerful key (§5 "No escalation"): the scopes, `daily_unit_cap`,
`allowed_images` and `expires_at` of the new key are bounded by the caller's.

201.description: The key, shown only this once, and its metadata (flat).

403.description: `forbidden`: the key lacks the admin scope. `escalation_denied`: the request asks for more than the calling key has (scopes, `daily_unit_cap`, `allowed_images` or `expires_at`); `errors` lists the fields.

422.description: Invalid body. `expires_at` must be in the future and in whole seconds (no fractional part).

delete.summary: Revokes a key of the caller's account. Idempotent.
delete.description:
A key can revoke itself, or any key it could have created (§5 "Revoking"). The account's last live unrestricted
admin key (no expiry, no cap, no image list) cannot be revoked.

403.description: `forbidden`: the key lacks the admin scope. `escalation_denied`: the target has more power than the calling key, so the calling key could not have created it; `errors` lists the fields.

404.description: No such key in this account.

409.description: `last_admin_key`: it is the account's last live unrestricted admin key (no expiry, no cap, no image list). Recover with `p2pc-server keys recover` if every admin key is lost.

get.summary: The account's nodes, in enrollment order.

parameters.name: state
parameters.description: Only nodes in this state: `online` (draining nodes included) or `offline`.

400.description: Invalid query string (for example an unknown `state`).

403.description: The key lacks the nodes:read scope.

get.summary: The account's join tokens, in creation order. Never contains a token or a code.

403.description: The key lacks the admin scope.

post.summary: Creates a single-use join token. The token is in the response, once.

201.description: The token (`p2pc_join_…`), shown only this once.

401.description: Missing or invalid key (also when the key was revoked or expired during the request).

403.description: The key lacks the admin scope.

delete.summary: Revokes an unused join token. Idempotent.

401.description: Missing or invalid key (also when the key was revoked or expired during the request).

403.description: The key lacks the admin scope.

404.description: No such token in this account.

409.description: `token_consumed`: a node already joined with it; delete the node instead.

403.description: The key lacks the nodes:read scope.

404.description: No such node in this account.

delete.summary: Deletes the node: closes its live connection, and its NodeId is no longer enrolled (`not_enrolled`).

403.description: The key lacks the nodes:write scope.

404.description: No such node in this account.

post.summary: Stops giving the node new leases, and tells it `Drain` when it is connected. Idempotent.

403.description: The key lacks the nodes:write scope.

404.description: No such node in this account.

post.summary: Lets the node take leases again, and tells it `Resume` when it is connected. Idempotent.

404.description: No such node in this account.

get.summary: The OpenAPI 3.1 document of this API.
The server's iroh NodeId, relays, address (`p2pc_srv_…`) and version.

200.description: How to reach this server over iroh.

get.summary:
The usage of the caller's project: finished attempts that ended in `[from, to)`, grouped by `group_by`, with
cursor pagination over the groups and the total of the whole range. Only the caller's own account and project
are ever counted.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: Start of the range (RFC 3339, inclusive). Default: the start of the current UTC day, or one day before `to`.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: End of the range (RFC 3339, exclusive). Default: one day after `from`.

200.description: The grouped usage and the total of the range.

400.description: Invalid query string (for example an unknown `group_by`).

403.description: The key lacks `jobs:read`.

get.summary:
Who the presented key is, and its limits. `daily_unit_cap: null` means the key is uncapped; `p2pc mcp` refuses
such a key. Never contains the secret.

200.description: The key's account, project, ID, scopes and limits (`label`, `daily_unit_cap`, `allowed_images`, `expires_at`; `null` means no limit). Never the secret.

ApiKeyInfo.description: An API key as listed by `GET /v1/keys`. Never contains the secret.

oneOf.description: Daily cap in milli-units.

last_used_at.description: Last time the key authenticated a request (the server writes it at most once a minute).

revoked_at.description: When the key was revoked. A revoked key's row is never deleted (§5).

AuditEvent.description:
One row of the append-only audit log, as returned by `GET /v1/audit` (§5 "Audit").

`detail` is a JSON object that **never holds a secret**: no key, token, code or env value. The server should
check it with [`audit_detail_has_secret`] before writing.

oneOf.description:
The device that acted, if any (H2 §5.6). At most one of `actor_key_id` and `actor_device_id` is set. Left
out when `null`.
The key that acted, if any.

at.description: When it happened (the start of the minute, for `auth_failed`).

subject_id.description: The object acted on (a key, join token or node ID), as an opaque string.

AuditKind.description: What an audit event records (§5 "Audit"). Closed: one value per event the spec lists.

BlobInput.description:
A blob input (H2 §7.1): the blob, delivered read-only at `path`.

**Strict** (request type): the `POST /v1/jobs` body, and what the agent parses a lease's job into (`LeaseJob::parse_strict`). Unknown fields are rejected, which catches typos and refuses a lease the agent would not fully understand (§6). Responses use the lenient twin, [`JobSpecView`].

blob.description: The blob, which must exist in the caller's account when the job is created.

path.description: Absolute path under `/inputs/`, with the `files` path rules.

BlobInputView.description:
A blob input (H2 §7.1): the blob, delivered read-only at `path`.

**Lenient and redacted** (response type): the `spec` of a [`Job`] in API responses (§7 "Job representation in responses"). Unknown fields are ignored, so an older CLI or SDK keeps reading jobs after the server adds a field (§6). `env` values are always `"<redacted>"` and `files` carry `{path, size, sha256}` with no content, and there is **no `idempotency_key`**: a response never carries it (§7). Build it with [`JobSpecView::from_stored`].

blob.description: The blob, which must exist in the caller's account when the job is created.

path.description: Absolute path under `/inputs/`, with the `files` path rules.

BlobRef.description: A blob input's content address (H2 §7.1, §7.5): `sha256:<64 lowercase hex>`.

disk_mb.description:
Disk for job directories, in MiB (§6 `Inventory`, §8). `None` when the agent does not report it (older than
the 2026-11-07 amendment): the scheduler then places by CPU, memory and GPU only.

allowed_images.description: Glob patterns on the normalized image reference. `None` allows every image.

oneOf.description: Daily cap in milli-units, per UTC day.

expires_at.description: Optional expiry (§5). After it, the key authenticates nothing.

label.description: Optional human label, shown when tokens are listed.

pre_approved.description:
The node it enrolls starts `approved` (H2 §5.4, §5.5). `admin` principals only (else `403`). Left out when
`false`.

ttl_s.description:
Validity in seconds. Default 900 (15 minutes), maximum 86 400 (24 h); at most 900 with `pre_approved`, and
for a `nodes:join` principal (H2 §7.3, where the spec calls it `expires_in_s`).

DeviceId.description: Identifies a paired device (`dev_…`, H2 §5.5): a principal like an API key, authenticated by its iroh NodeId.

Egress.description:
Network egress policy.

allow.description: Allowed domains. Each one matches itself and its subdomains on whole labels.

EgressView.description:
Network egress policy.

Build it with [`JobSpecView::from_stored`].

allow.description: Allowed domains. Each one matches itself and its subdomains on whole labels.

ErrorCode.description: A stable, machine-readable validation error code.

feasible.description: Whether some enrolled node could ever run the job.

reason.description: Why the job is not feasible, or would queue.

units_per_hour.description: Units the job reserves per hour, in milli-units.

would_queue.description: Whether the job would wait in the queue right now.

field.description: Path of the offending field, for example `resources.cpu` or `files[0].path`.

message.description: Human explanation. Never contains env values or file contents.

GpuInfo.description: One GPU (§6 "GPU inventory"). The `uuid` is its key: a GPU is never identified by its index.

compute_capability.description: Compute capability, for example `8.9`, if known.

cuda_driver_version.description: CUDA version the driver supports, if known.

index.description: Device index as the driver enumerates it. Informational only.

mig.description: Whether MIG is enabled. A MIG card is reported but not offerable in v0.1.

pci_bdf.description: PCI bus/device/function, for example `0000:01:00.0`, if known (not on WSL2).

vram_mb.description: Video memory in MiB. `None` means unknown, and then the GPU is not offerable (it is never guessed).

GpuStatus.description: GPU detection status with an optional explanation.

Health.description: Response of `GET /healthz` (§7): liveness only, with no data.

HealthCheck.description:
A service health check (H2 §7.1): exactly one of `http_get` or `tcp: true`.

**Strict** (request type): the `POST /v1/jobs` body, and what the agent parses a lease's job into (`LeaseJob::parse_strict`). Unknown fields are rejected, which catches typos and refuses a lease the agent would not fully understand (§6). Responses use the lenient twin, [`JobSpecView`].

failure_threshold.description: Consecutive failed checks that make it `unhealthy`, 1-20. Default 3.

http_get.description: An absolute path to `GET`, at most 256 bytes. Only the status line is read.

port.description: The port to check: one of `service.ports`.

start_period_s.description: Seconds the service may stay `starting`, 0-3 600. Default 300.

timeout_s.description: Seconds before one check fails, 1-60. Default 3.

HealthCheckView.description:
A service health check (H2 §7.1): exactly one of `http_get` or `tcp: true`.

Unknown fields are ignored, so an older CLI or SDK keeps reading jobs after the server adds a field (§6). `env` values are always `"<redacted>"` and `files` carry `{path, size, sha256}` with no content, and there is **no `idempotency_key`**: a response never carries it (§7). InputFile.description:
An input file in a request: written to `path` (under `/inputs`) with the base64-decoded `content_b64`.

`Debug` shows the path and the encoded length, never the content. **Strict** (request type): unknown fields are
rejected.

content_b64.description: File content, standard base64 with padding.

InputFileView.description:
An input file as shown in responses (§7): its path, decoded size and SHA-256, **never its content**. Lenient:
unknown fields are ignored.

Inventory.description:
What a node has (§6 `Join`/`Hello`, §7 `GET /v1/nodes`). Reported by the agent; validate it with
[`crate::protocol::validate_inventory`] when it comes from the network.

disk_total_mb.description:
Size of the filesystem that holds the job directories, in MiB, if the agent could read it. `offered.disk_mb`
never exceeds it (validated).

dxg.description: Whether `/dev/dxg` (the WSL2 GPU device) is present.

hostname.description:
The machine's hostname, as reported. The server derives the node's unique `name` from it (§5); it is never
used for authentication.

offered.description: Capacity offered to jobs: hardware × the owner's share limits (§8).

platform.description: Native Linux or the WSL2 distro.

oneOf.description: WSL2 health block; absent on native Linux.

Job.description: A job as returned by the API.

attempt.description: Current attempt, starting at 1 (0 while never placed).

attempts.description:
The job's attempts, oldest first: only in `GET /v1/jobs/{id}`; lists of jobs leave the field out (§7). An
attempt is an accepted lease: refused or unanswered offers are not listed.

cancel_requested_at.description:
When a cancel was requested for a job that was already `assigned` or `running` (the scheduler delivers it to
the node, and the job ends `cancelled`). `null` if none was requested, or if the job was queued and
cancelled at once.

error.description: Short error code when the job failed without an exit code (for example `disk_limit`).

estimated_units.description: Estimated units reserved by the job (resources × timeout).

exit_code.description: Exit code, when the job exited.

finished_at.description: When the job reached a terminal state.

name.description: Optional label, copied from the spec.

oneOf.description: Node of the current or last attempt.

reason.description:
Why the job is in its current state, when there is something to tell the user, for example why a queued job
is not being placed (§8 "Offer cap"). User-visible; never contains secrets.

oneOf.description:
The service view of a `kind = "service"` job (H2 §7.2): health, ports, idle and cap deadlines, the hub's model
pull and today's traffic. Left out for batch jobs.

spec.description:
The submitted spec, with the image normalized, built with [`JobSpecView::from_stored`]: `env` values are
`"<redacted>"` and files carry no content (§7). Lenient: a field added by a newer server does not break
older clients.

started_at.description: When the current attempt started running.

JobAttempt.description: One attempt of a job, in `GET /v1/jobs/{id}` (§7): an accepted lease, on one node.

attempt.description: The attempt number, from 1. Only node loss starts a new one.

ended_at.description: When the attempt ended; `null` while it runs.

outcome.description:
In job-state words: `running` while the attempt is in progress (accepted, or started), then `succeeded`,
`failed`, `timed_out`, `cancelled` or `lost`. An attempt replaced after node loss (fenced) is `lost`.

reason.description:
The reason code of the end (for example `exited_0`, `exit_code`, `node_lost`, `absent_from_hello`,
`watchdog`), or `null` while the attempt runs. Never a secret.

started_at.description:
When the job process started on the node (`JobStarted`); `null` if it never did (accepted, then lost or timed
out during the image pull).

JobKind.description:
What kind of job a spec describes (H2 §7.1): a batch job runs to completion (H1), a service keeps running and
exposes ports. `batch` is the default, and is left out of serialized specs, so H1 peers see H1 bytes.

JobSpec.description:
A job specification: what to run and with which limits (§7, H2 §7.1).

`Debug` never prints environment values or input file contents (§7: env values are never logged).

**Strict** (request type): the `POST /v1/jobs` body, and what the agent parses a lease's job into (`LeaseJob::parse_strict`). Unknown fields are rejected, which catches typos and refuses a lease the agent would not fully understand (§6). Responses use the lenient twin, [`JobSpecView`].

command.description: The argv to run. There is no shell unless the argv calls one.

egress.description: Network egress allowlist. Empty means no network at all.

env.description:
Environment variables. Values are secret-like: never logged, and never returned by the API.

Values may not contain NUL, `\n` or `\r` (§7): they go into Podman's line-based `--env-file`, where a
newline would inject another variable. Encode multi-line secrets as base64, or pass them as `files`.

files.description: Files written under `/inputs` before the job starts.

idempotency_key.description:
Client-chosen key that makes the submission idempotent (§7). Scoped to the principal that submits
it, an API key or a device (H2 §5.6). It is **never returned**: no response type has it (see
[`JobSpecView`]).

outputs.description: Limits on the files collected from `/outputs`.

retry.description:
Retry policy. For `batch`, only node loss consumes an attempt (default 2); for `service`, it counts
consecutive attempts that never became healthy (default 3).

oneOf.description: The service block: required when `kind = "service"`, forbidden otherwise (H2 §7.1).

Read-only: set by a template launch (H2 §7.6). A `POST /v1/jobs` that sends it gets
`422 read_only_field`.

timeout_s.description:
Wall-clock limit in seconds. Every job has one (hard rule 3). Default 3 600 for `batch` (1-86 400) and
2 592 000, 30 days, for `service` (60-2 592 000). (`serde(default)` here only marks it optional in the
schema: deserialization goes through the wire type, which applies the default of the `kind`.)

volumes.description: Persistent volumes, 0-4 (H2 §7.1, §11.3): only for services and template launches.

JobStatus.description:
State of a job (§7).

`queued → assigned → running → {succeeded | failed | timed_out | cancelled | lost}`, with requeueing on node loss.
See [`transition_allowed`].

JoinTokenId.description: Identifies a join token row (`jtk_…`), as listed and revoked by the admin API (§5). Never the token itself.

JoinTokenInfo.description:
A join token as listed by `GET /v1/nodes/join-tokens` (§5 "Listing and revoking"). Never contains the token or
its code.
